./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/doi_cache.json:293:    "abstract": "With the widespread adoption of social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter, online communication has become an integral part of everyday life. However, this digital transformation has also led to the emergence of cyberbullying, a serious social issue affecting individuals across all age groups,particularly adolescents. Cyberbullying involves the use of electronic communication to harass, threaten, or humiliate individuals, often leading to severe psychological consequences such as anxiety, depression, and, in extreme cases, suicidal tendencies. Detecting cyberbullying manually is a complex and time-consuming task due to the massive volume of usergenerated content and the subtle, context-dependent nature of abusive language. This research proposes a machine learning and natural language processing (NLP)-based approach to automatically detect cyberbullying in social media text. The study utilizes text preprocessing techniques and implements classification algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest.The performance of these models is evaluated using standard metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The findings indicate that machine learning-based models can effectively identify bullying content, making them a promising solution for enhancing online safety and moderating harmful interactions on digital platforms. Keywords: Cyberbullying Detection, Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Social Media Analysis, Text Classification.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/doi_cache.json:546:    "abstract": "Machine Learning is present in our lives now more than ever. One of the most researched areas in machine learning is focused on creating systems that are able to understand natural language. Natural language processing is a broad domain, having a vast number of applications with a significant impact in society. In our current era, we rely on tools that can ease our lives. We can search through thousands of documents to find something that we need, but this can take a lot of time. Having a system that can understand a simple query and return only relevant documents is more efficient. Although current approaches are well capable of understanding natural language, there is still space for improvement. This thesis studies multiple natural language processing tasks, presenting approaches on applications such as information retrieval, polarity detection, dialect identification [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2018], automatic essay scoring [Cozma et al., 2018], and methods that can help other systems to understand documents better. Part of the described approaches from this thesis are employing kernel methods, especially string kernels. A method based on string kernels that can determine in what dialect a document is written is presented in this thesis. The approach is treating texts at the character level, extracting features in the form of p -grams of characters, and combining several kernels, including presence bits kernel and intersection kernel. Kernel methods are also presented as a solution for defining the complexity of a specific word. By combining multiple low-level features and high-level semantic features, the approach can find if a non-native speaker of a language can see a word as complicated or not. With one focus on string kernels, this thesis proposes two transductive methods that can improve the results obtained by employing string kernels. One approach suggests using the pairwise string kernel similarities between samples from the training and test sets as features. The other method defines a simple self-training algorithm composed of two iterations. As usual, a classifier is trained over the training data, then is it used to predict the labels of the test samples. In the second iteration, the algorithm adds a predefined number of test samples to the training set for another round of training. These two transductive methods work by adapting the learning method to the test set. A novel cross-dialectal corpus is shown in this thesis. The Moldavian versus Romanian Corpus (MOROCO) [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2019a] contains over 30.000 samples collected from the news domain, split across six categories. Several studies can be employed over this corpus such as binary classification between Romanian and Moldavian samples, intra-dialect multi-class categorization by topic, and cross-dialect multi-class classification by topic. Two baseline approaches are presented for this collection of texts. One method is based on a simple string kernel model. The second approach consists of a character-level deep neural network, which includes several Squeeze-and-Excitation Blocks (SE-blocks). As known at this moment, this is the first time when a SE-block is employed in a natural language processing context. This thesis also presents a method for German Dialect Identification composed on a voting scheme that combines a Character-level Convolutional Neural Network, a Long Short-Term Memory Network, and a model based on String Kernels. Word sense disambiguation is still one of the challenges of the NLP domain. In this context, this thesis tackles this challenge and presents a novel disambiguation algorithm, known as ShowtgunWSD [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2019b]. By treating the global disambiguation problem as multiple local disambiguation problems, ShotgunWSD is capable of determining the sense of the words in an unsupervised and deterministic way, using WordNet as a resource. For this method to work, three functions that can compute the similarity between two words senses are defined. The disambiguation algorithm works as follows. The document is split into multiple windows of words of a specific size for each window. After that, a brute-force algorithm that computes every combination of senses for each word within that window is employed. For every window combination, a score is calculated using one of the three similarity functions. The last step merges the windows using a prefix and suffix matching to form more significant and relevant windows. In the end, the formed windows are ranked by the length and score, and the top ones, based on a voting scheme, will determine the sense for each word. Documents can contain a variable number of words, therefore employing them in machine learning may be hard at times. This thesis presents two novel approaches [Ionescu and Butnaru, 2019] that can represent documents using a finite number of features. Both methods are inspired by computer vision, and they work by first transforming the words within documents to a word representation, such as word2vec. Having words represented in this way, a k-means clustering algorithm can be applied over the words. The centroids of the formed clusters are gathered into a vocabulary. Each word from a document is then represented by the closest centroid from the previously formed vocabulary. To this point, both methods share the same steps. One approach is designed to compute the final representation of a document by calculating the frequency of each centroid found inside it. This method is named Bag of Super Word Embeddings (BOSWE) because each centroid can be viewed as a super word. The second approach presented in this thesis, known as Vector of Locally-Aggregated Word Embeddings (VLAWE), computes the document representation by accumulating the differences between each centroid and each word vector associated with the respective centroid. This thesis also describes a new way to score essays automatically by combining a low-level string kernel model with a high-level semantic feature representation, namely the BOSWE representation. The methods described in this thesis exhibit state-of-the-art performance levels over multiple tasks. One fact to support this claim is that the string kernel method employed for Arabic Dialect Identification obtained the first place, two years in a row at the Fourth and Fifth Workshop on NLP for Similar Languages, Varieties, and Dialects (VarDial). The same string kernel model obtained the fifth place at the German Dialect Identification Closed Shared Task at VarDial Workshop of EACL 2017. Second of all, the Complex Word Identification model scored a third-place at the CWI Shared Task of the BEA-13 of NAACL 2018. Third of all, it is worth to mention that the ShotgunWSD algorithm surpassed the MCS baseline on several datasets. Lastly, the model that combines string kernel and bag of super word embeddings obtained state-of-the-art performance over the Automated Student Assessment Prize dataset.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/doi_cache.json:673:    "abstract": "Our research examines how Natural Language Processing and Deep Learning methods help learners better understand foreign languages and cultures. Our research showed that advanced language technology tools including machine translation speech recognition and sentiment analysis help students learn both language skills and cultural understanding better. Our research team tested 100 participants across English, Chinese, and Spanish with 50 participants in each group. The experimental group studied with NLP and DL platform-based language learning platforms but the control group used traditional education methods. Researchers tested cultural knowledge and language skills for 12 weeks by giving tests before and after the experiment. The experimental group made better progress in speaking English (35%) and understanding Chinese culture (45%) compared to the control group. The learning system used NLP and DL tools to provide real-time feedback and context analysis which improved both the personalization and depth of the educational experience. These technologies show how they can enhance language and cultural learning in modern education so students benefit from them.",
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/doi_cache.json:690:    "abstract": "Purpose This study aims to provide an overview of recent efforts relating to natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning applied to archival processing, particularly appraisal and sensitivity reviews, and propose functional requirements and workflow considerations for transitioning from experimental to operational use of these tools. Design/methodology/approach The paper has four main sections. 1) A short overview of the NLP and machine learning concepts referenced in the paper. 2) A review of the literature reporting on NLP and machine learning applied to archival processes. 3) An overview and commentary on key existing and developing tools that use NLP or machine learning techniques for archives. 4) This review and analysis will inform a discussion of functional requirements and workflow considerations for NLP and machine learning tools for archival processing. Findings Applications for processing e-mail have received the most attention so far, although most initiatives have been experimental or project based. It now seems feasible to branch out to develop more generalized tools for born-digital, unstructured records. Effective NLP and machine learning tools for archival processing should be usable, interoperable, flexible, iterative and configurable. Originality/value Most implementations of NLP for archives have been experimental or project based. The main exception that has moved into production is ePADD, which includes robust NLP features through its named entity recognition module. This paper takes a broader view, assessing the prospects and possible directions for integrating NLP tools and techniques into archival workflows.",

./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:2:title: "Exercise Interventions and Depressive Symptoms in Older Adults: An Abstract-Level Random-Effects Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trial Evidence"
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:35:  - random-effects meta-analysis
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:74: The workflow is summarized conceptually in @fig-method and as a screening flow in @fig-prisma; the main pooled result is summarized in @fig-forest and @tbl-main. The analysis uses the available abstract-level evidence to estimate the direction and uncertainty of exercise effects on depressive symptoms among older adults. It also treats heterogeneity as a central result rather than a nuisance. When exercise formats, populations, outcome instruments, comparators, and reporting practices differ, a random-effects model can summarize the evidence, but the summary must remain cautious.
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:76:![Overview of the abstract-level meta-analysis pipeline.](figures/fig_method_overview.png){#fig-method}
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:143:The study used an OpenAlex abstract-level workflow recorded in `real_experiments/real_results.json`. The evidence source is recorded as literature, and the synthesis lane is recorded as intervention meta-analysis. The workflow identified `66618` records and scanned `2400` abstract records. All `2400` scanned records had abstract text available. The source channel recorded for the scanned abstracts was Europe PMC. The search and screening yield is summarized in @tbl-search-screening and visualized in @fig-prisma.
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:162:@fig-method summarizes the conceptual workflow from search, through PICO screening, to extraction and scale-specific synthesis. The figure should be read as a methodological schematic rather than as an additional source of numerical evidence. Its purpose is to show why the design produces a bounded evidence product: the analysis begins with a large bibliographic surface, narrows through abstract language, extracts only reported quantitative effects, and pools only effects that are comparable on the standardized mean difference scale.
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:177:The extraction rule followed the principle that direction and scale must be interpretable before pooling. For the main standardized mean difference analysis, negative values were interpreted as lower depressive symptom scores for exercise relative to comparator when the abstract-level source used that direction. Because abstract-level reporting can omit details about scale orientation, comparator construction, or outcome timing, the pooled estimate is interpreted cautiously even when the sign is favorable.
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:181:The main analysis used DerSimonian-Laird random effects for the workflow-selected standardized mean differences. This model was chosen because the literature and the extracted abstracts span diverse exercise formats, older-adult populations, comparators, and outcome scales. The main synthesis used `k = 8` standardized mean difference inputs. The pooled standardized mean difference was `-0.4327`, with confidence interval `-0.9057` to `0.0402`. Heterogeneity was high, with `I2 = 95.4`, `tau2 = 0.4254`, and `Q = 150.871`. These values are reported in @tbl-main and displayed in @fig-forest.
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:194:The methods intentionally privilege reproducibility and explicit scope over maximal clinical detail. Abstract-level synthesis can efficiently map a large evidence surface, but it cannot resolve all trial-level questions. It cannot verify all intervention components, comparator details, outcome hierarchies, participant overlap, or analytic choices that may be available only in full text. The analysis therefore estimates direction and uncertainty under a constrained extraction design. It does not provide treatment recommendations, and it does not supersede systematic reviews that retrieve full reports, assess risk of bias, and conduct protocol-defined subgroup or sensitivity analyses [@li2024; @tian2024; @cheng2025; @yan2026; @atchison2025].
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:208:The inventory is important because it prevents a common interpretive error. The presence of `58` extracted effects does not mean that all extracted effects are directly poolable in a single model. Pooling across incompatible effect scales would create an estimate that is harder to interpret than the underlying abstracts. The analysis therefore separates extraction breadth from synthesis comparability. The broad inventory documents what the abstract-level workflow found; the main pooled result answers the narrower standardized mean difference question.
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:238:The findings also clarify how abstract-level synthesis can complement existing reviews. Full-text reviews and network meta-analyses remain necessary for intervention-specific inference, comparator ranking, risk-of-bias assessment, dose-response modeling, and subgroup analysis [@tian2024; @atchison2025; @zhu2025; @dai2025]. The present synthesis offers a different product: a bounded pooled estimate whose point estimate favors exercise in direction but whose 95% confidence interval includes the null, leaving the magnitude, statistical reliability, and external validity uncertain. That product can help frame future full-text reviews, identify where abstract reporting is insufficient, and prevent overconfident claims from a heterogeneous evidence base.
./jobs/v2_2948a09a83a9/run/paper_springer.qmd:264:This abstract-level random-effects meta-analysis found a directionally favorable but not statistically significant pooled standardized mean difference for exercise interventions on depressive symptoms in older adults, with a confidence interval that included the null and substantial heterogeneity. The workflow documented a large evidence surface, a narrower extractable abstract-level set, and a main pooled estimate that is useful for feasibility and uncertainty assessment. The results should not be interpreted as definitive clinical guidance. Instead, they suggest that the abstract-level evidence is compatible with a possible benefit of exercise, but the non-significant pooled estimate, high heterogeneity, and small `k = 8` main synthesis require future full-text synthesis to examine modality, dose, comparator, population, and outcome timing in greater detail.

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/metadata.json:33:    "abstract": "With the escalating need to derive and evaluate subjective information from social media platforms such as Twitter, where millions of Twitter users update their tweets in the form of textual data every day, the application of Sentiment Analysis becomes even more relevant. This paper proposes an integrated system by integrating the applications of NLP and ML techniques to classify and derive the sentiment and psychological indicators of users instantaneously and with higher accuracy and explainability. For the instant derivation of sentiment polarity and psychological indicators with better accuracy, the proposed system uses TF-IDF feature extraction with Logistic Regression classification. In addition, it uses VADER sentiment analyzer that gives an instant rule-based classification of emotional tone of given text. The proposed system includes a number of preprocessing stages of data such as microtext normalization, tokenization, removal of stopwords and lemmatization. The proposed system is implemented and the results indicate that the proposed lightweight and interpretable approach obtains performance close to the state-of-the-art while maintaining the lowest computational cost. The proposed system is showcased via the development of a Streamlit-based web application to make the system user-friendly for researchers, practitioners as well as for the public. The derived system can instantaneously classify any text to positive, negative, neutral sentiments and also derive the psychological indicators of users related to mental health such as anxiety, sadness and also depression. Hence, the proposed system bridges the existing gap between research prototypes and practical applications with respect to social media sentiment analysis.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/metadata.json:72:    "abstract": "The article presents a study on the practical application of vectorization methods in natural language processing tasks using machine learning. The main purpose of the work is to implement and evaluate the effectiveness of vector texts representations in order to classify mathematical texts by subject matter. One-hot encoding, Bag of Words, and TF-IDF implemented in Python using Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and scikit-learn libraries are considered as vectorization methods. A pipeline of text data preprocessing, vectorization and classification based on a decision tree has been developed. The analysis of the results showed that the TF-IDF method allows taking into account rare but semantically significant terms, which contributes to a better separation of documents into mathematical areas. The scientific novelty is represented by the adaptation of classical vectorization methods to a highly specialized corpus of mathematical texts, and this field was not previously sufficiently covered in the research. The article demonstrates the practical value of the integration of thew natural language processing methods with machine learning for domain-oriented categorization of scientific texts and opens up prospects for further research in this area.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/metadata.json:198:    "abstract": "The gradual adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) globally serves as a crucial move toward addressing global decarbonization goals for sustainable development. However, the lack of cost-effective, power-efficient, and safe chargers for EV batteries hampers adoption. Understanding the research needs and identifying the gaps in EV charger innovation informs investments and research to address development challenges. This study developed a unique text mining workflow to classify themes in EV charger technology and product development by analyzing U.S. patent award summaries. The text mining workflow combined the techniques of data extraction, data cleaning, natural language processing (NLP), statistical analysis, and unsupervised machine learning (ML) to extract unique themes and to visualize their relationships. There was a 47.7% increase in the number of EV charger patents issued in 2022 relative to that in 2018. The top four themes were charging station management, power transfer efficiency, on-board charger design, and temperature management. More than half (53.8%) of the EV charger patents issued over the five-year period from 2018 to 2022 addressed problems within those four themes. Patents that addressed wireless charging, fast charging, and fleet charging accounted for less than 10% each of the EV charger patents issued. This suggests that the industry is still at the frontier of addressing those problems. This study further presents examples of the specific EV charger problems addressed within each theme. The findings can inform investment decisions and policymaking to focus on R\\&D resources that will advance the state of the art and spur EV adoption.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/metadata.json:215:    "abstract": "Recent progress in NLP has led to an importance of good text data classification with suitable machine learning algorithms over numerous domains. In a vast variety of NLP applications such as sentiment analysis, document categorization, topic modeling, text classification task is extremely important. Here, in terms of machine learning approach Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, have been broadly employed; their relative superiority also continues to be the concern of recent research work. In order to appraise and compare the three performance parameters of the three dominant algorithms being selected (Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and SVM for the text classification problem from synthetic datasets) is the main aim in a given task. Three different categories are involved, one each for Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Natural Language Processing (NLP), by applying the algorithms, obtaining their accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.This paper has utilized a dataset of 1,000 labeled sentences into three classes, AI, ML, and NLP, in predefined categories. A rigorous methodology in this study will cover the steps of acquiring the data, preprocessing the same, extraction of the feature set by TF-IDF vectorization, and reducing dimensionality with the help of Truncated SVD. This work applies three models, namely Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and SVM, and has evaluated the performances by means of accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC.Results have shown that Naive Bayes performed excellent with accuracy at 94% while maintaining high precision, recall, and F1-score values for all categories. Both Random Forest and SVM are performing well; however, the Naive Bayes training time and efficiency were highly superior. High discriminative powers of Naive Bayes have been further verified by the AUC-ROC score, and high-dimensional, complex data handling is very robust in Random Forest. This study confirms that Naive Bayes performs effectively in accuracy and efficiency when applied to tasks of text classification, outperforming Random Forest and SVM results in the metrics used for evaluation. The results indicate that although the performance of the two latter are competitive, the Naive Bayes stays as one of the favorite candidates for use in text classification tasks that demand speed coupled with precision.This research contributes towards the ongoing discourse in NLP by providing a comparison of three widely used ML algorithms in text classification; thus, it provides deep insights into the strengths as well as limitations of each, thus assisting in the choosing of the most appropriate model for the task of the application in NLP-related tasks. The findings indicate that choosing the right criteria of evaluation is also key in completely assessing the adequacy of the model to achieve its intended purpose and outcome.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/metadata.json:293:    "abstract": "With the widespread adoption of social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter, online communication has become an integral part of everyday life. However, this digital transformation has also led to the emergence of cyberbullying, a serious social issue affecting individuals across all age groups,particularly adolescents. Cyberbullying involves the use of electronic communication to harass, threaten, or humiliate individuals, often leading to severe psychological consequences such as anxiety, depression, and, in extreme cases, suicidal tendencies. Detecting cyberbullying manually is a complex and time-consuming task due to the massive volume of usergenerated content and the subtle, context-dependent nature of abusive language. This research proposes a machine learning and natural language processing (NLP)-based approach to automatically detect cyberbullying in social media text. The study utilizes text preprocessing techniques and implements classification algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest.The performance of these models is evaluated using standard metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The findings indicate that machine learning-based models can effectively identify bullying content, making them a promising solution for enhancing online safety and moderating harmful interactions on digital platforms. Keywords: Cyberbullying Detection, Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Social Media Analysis, Text Classification.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/metadata.json:546:    "abstract": "Machine Learning is present in our lives now more than ever. One of the most researched areas in machine learning is focused on creating systems that are able to understand natural language. Natural language processing is a broad domain, having a vast number of applications with a significant impact in society. In our current era, we rely on tools that can ease our lives. We can search through thousands of documents to find something that we need, but this can take a lot of time. Having a system that can understand a simple query and return only relevant documents is more efficient. Although current approaches are well capable of understanding natural language, there is still space for improvement. This thesis studies multiple natural language processing tasks, presenting approaches on applications such as information retrieval, polarity detection, dialect identification [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2018], automatic essay scoring [Cozma et al., 2018], and methods that can help other systems to understand documents better. Part of the described approaches from this thesis are employing kernel methods, especially string kernels. A method based on string kernels that can determine in what dialect a document is written is presented in this thesis. The approach is treating texts at the character level, extracting features in the form of p -grams of characters, and combining several kernels, including presence bits kernel and intersection kernel. Kernel methods are also presented as a solution for defining the complexity of a specific word. By combining multiple low-level features and high-level semantic features, the approach can find if a non-native speaker of a language can see a word as complicated or not. With one focus on string kernels, this thesis proposes two transductive methods that can improve the results obtained by employing string kernels. One approach suggests using the pairwise string kernel similarities between samples from the training and test sets as features. The other method defines a simple self-training algorithm composed of two iterations. As usual, a classifier is trained over the training data, then is it used to predict the labels of the test samples. In the second iteration, the algorithm adds a predefined number of test samples to the training set for another round of training. These two transductive methods work by adapting the learning method to the test set. A novel cross-dialectal corpus is shown in this thesis. The Moldavian versus Romanian Corpus (MOROCO) [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2019a] contains over 30.000 samples collected from the news domain, split across six categories. Several studies can be employed over this corpus such as binary classification between Romanian and Moldavian samples, intra-dialect multi-class categorization by topic, and cross-dialect multi-class classification by topic. Two baseline approaches are presented for this collection of texts. One method is based on a simple string kernel model. The second approach consists of a character-level deep neural network, which includes several Squeeze-and-Excitation Blocks (SE-blocks). As known at this moment, this is the first time when a SE-block is employed in a natural language processing context. This thesis also presents a method for German Dialect Identification composed on a voting scheme that combines a Character-level Convolutional Neural Network, a Long Short-Term Memory Network, and a model based on String Kernels. Word sense disambiguation is still one of the challenges of the NLP domain. In this context, this thesis tackles this challenge and presents a novel disambiguation algorithm, known as ShowtgunWSD [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2019b]. By treating the global disambiguation problem as multiple local disambiguation problems, ShotgunWSD is capable of determining the sense of the words in an unsupervised and deterministic way, using WordNet as a resource. For this method to work, three functions that can compute the similarity between two words senses are defined. The disambiguation algorithm works as follows. The document is split into multiple windows of words of a specific size for each window. After that, a brute-force algorithm that computes every combination of senses for each word within that window is employed. For every window combination, a score is calculated using one of the three similarity functions. The last step merges the windows using a prefix and suffix matching to form more significant and relevant windows. In the end, the formed windows are ranked by the length and score, and the top ones, based on a voting scheme, will determine the sense for each word. Documents can contain a variable number of words, therefore employing them in machine learning may be hard at times. This thesis presents two novel approaches [Ionescu and Butnaru, 2019] that can represent documents using a finite number of features. Both methods are inspired by computer vision, and they work by first transforming the words within documents to a word representation, such as word2vec. Having words represented in this way, a k-means clustering algorithm can be applied over the words. The centroids of the formed clusters are gathered into a vocabulary. Each word from a document is then represented by the closest centroid from the previously formed vocabulary. To this point, both methods share the same steps. One approach is designed to compute the final representation of a document by calculating the frequency of each centroid found inside it. This method is named Bag of Super Word Embeddings (BOSWE) because each centroid can be viewed as a super word. The second approach presented in this thesis, known as Vector of Locally-Aggregated Word Embeddings (VLAWE), computes the document representation by accumulating the differences between each centroid and each word vector associated with the respective centroid. This thesis also describes a new way to score essays automatically by combining a low-level string kernel model with a high-level semantic feature representation, namely the BOSWE representation. The methods described in this thesis exhibit state-of-the-art performance levels over multiple tasks. One fact to support this claim is that the string kernel method employed for Arabic Dialect Identification obtained the first place, two years in a row at the Fourth and Fifth Workshop on NLP for Similar Languages, Varieties, and Dialects (VarDial). The same string kernel model obtained the fifth place at the German Dialect Identification Closed Shared Task at VarDial Workshop of EACL 2017. Second of all, the Complex Word Identification model scored a third-place at the CWI Shared Task of the BEA-13 of NAACL 2018. Third of all, it is worth to mention that the ShotgunWSD algorithm surpassed the MCS baseline on several datasets. Lastly, the model that combines string kernel and bag of super word embeddings obtained state-of-the-art performance over the Automated Student Assessment Prize dataset.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/metadata.json:673:    "abstract": "Our research examines how Natural Language Processing and Deep Learning methods help learners better understand foreign languages and cultures. Our research showed that advanced language technology tools including machine translation speech recognition and sentiment analysis help students learn both language skills and cultural understanding better. Our research team tested 100 participants across English, Chinese, and Spanish with 50 participants in each group. The experimental group studied with NLP and DL platform-based language learning platforms but the control group used traditional education methods. Researchers tested cultural knowledge and language skills for 12 weeks by giving tests before and after the experiment. The experimental group made better progress in speaking English (35%) and understanding Chinese culture (45%) compared to the control group. The learning system used NLP and DL tools to provide real-time feedback and context analysis which improved both the personalization and depth of the educational experience. These technologies show how they can enhance language and cultural learning in modern education so students benefit from them.",
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/metadata.json:690:    "abstract": "Purpose This study aims to provide an overview of recent efforts relating to natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning applied to archival processing, particularly appraisal and sensitivity reviews, and propose functional requirements and workflow considerations for transitioning from experimental to operational use of these tools. Design/methodology/approach The paper has four main sections. 1) A short overview of the NLP and machine learning concepts referenced in the paper. 2) A review of the literature reporting on NLP and machine learning applied to archival processes. 3) An overview and commentary on key existing and developing tools that use NLP or machine learning techniques for archives. 4) This review and analysis will inform a discussion of functional requirements and workflow considerations for NLP and machine learning tools for archival processing. Findings Applications for processing e-mail have received the most attention so far, although most initiatives have been experimental or project based. It now seems feasible to branch out to develop more generalized tools for born-digital, unstructured records. Effective NLP and machine learning tools for archival processing should be usable, interoperable, flexible, iterative and configurable. Originality/value Most implementations of NLP for archives have been experimental or project based. The main exception that has moved into production is ePADD, which includes robust NLP features through its named entity recognition module. This paper takes a broader view, assessing the prospects and possible directions for integrating NLP tools and techniques into archival workflows.",

In this study, primitive cases are considered that used crucial algorithms, and knowledge that can be opted for sentiment analysis. A survey of the work that has been done till now is conducted observing the results and outcomes concerning varying parameters of various researchers who worked on previously existing as well as novel and hybrid algorithms opting legion methodologies. The fundamental algorithms like Support Vector Machine (SVM), Bayesian Networks (BN), Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt), Conditional Random Fields (CRF) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are also discussed to achieve practice percentage and accuracy score in the field of NLP, sentiment analysis and text analytics. Various other novel approaches and algorithms like CNN, LSTM, KNN, K*, K‐means, K‐means++, SOM and ENORA, along with their limitations and the performance metrics providing accuracies for major open data sets are also analyzed.",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/phase1_concept.md:1:# Research Concept — LLM-Based Patent Analysis
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/phase1_concept.md:13:H3: A hybrid pipeline (LLM novelty scoring + PatentSBERTa retrieval) achieves the best overall performance across all patent analysis tasks.
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/phase1_concept.md:17:1. **Methodological**: First systematic benchmark comparing general-purpose LLMs (BERT, LLaMA, Qwen with LoRA) against domain-specific patent models (PatentBERT, PatentSBERTa) across three patent analysis tasks on the Harvard USPTO Patent Dataset (HUPD, 4.5M patents).
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/phase1_concept.md:19:2. **Empirical**: Comprehensive evaluation across patent acceptance prediction (binary), CPC classification (multi-label, 640+ classes), and prior art retrieval (ranking), with cost-performance analysis covering inference latency, training cost, and parameter efficiency.
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/phase1_concept.md:21:3. **Practical**: A hybrid patent analysis pipeline that combines LLM-based novelty scoring with domain-specific retrieval, providing actionable deployment guidance for patent offices and IP service providers.
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/phase1_concept.md:29:3. **Missing cost-performance analysis**: Patent offices face real computational constraints. No study quantifies the cost-performance tradeoff between lightweight domain-specific models and large LLMs for patent analysis tasks.

./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase3_positioning.md:7:**Delivery modality-focused evidence.** A growing number of meta-analyses restrict inclusion to a single delivery modality, reflecting the accelerating diversification of MBI formats in both research and practice. Reangsing et al. (2023) synthesised 15 randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of online MBIs and reported a moderate pooled effect on anxiety (Hedges' g = 0.46, 95% CI [0.29, 0.63]), but deliberately excluded face-to-face and hybrid formats, leaving cross-modality comparison outside the scope of their analysis. Similarly, Lee and Park (2025) conducted a meta-analysis of standalone digital mindfulness interventions, though their primary outcome was sleep rather than anxiety, and their sampling frame was likewise limited to a single delivery channel. These reviews establish that digitally delivered MBIs produce measurable anxiety reduction, but their modality-specific inclusion criteria prevent assessment of whether the effect magnitude differs systematically across delivery formats such as self-guided app-based programmes, guided online courses, and traditional face-to-face MBSR or MBCT groups.
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase3_positioning.md:9:**Population-condition-specific evidence.** A second stream targets narrow clinical or demographic subgroups, generating precise effect estimates for particular populations at the expense of generalisability across the broader adult spectrum. Ajele and Idemudia (2026) reported a stratified subgroup meta-analysis of MBIs for anxiety, depression, and stress among adults with cancer, finding a significant pooled reduction in anxiety (Hedges' g = 0.39, p < 0.001), while Virgili (2013) meta-analysed seven studies of MBIs in working adults and reported a moderate-to-large effect on psychological distress (d = 0.68). These estimates are internally valid for their respective populations, but the heterogeneity of effect sizes across studies—0.39 for cancer patients, 0.68 for working adults, 0.46 for online-only general adult samples (Reangsing et al., 2023)—cannot be disentangled from the population and modality confounds because no single analytic framework has coded both population and delivery type simultaneously.
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase3_positioning.md:11:**Comprehensive multi-outcome syntheses.** A smaller set of reviews adopts a broader scope, addressing multiple clinical outcomes and delivery formats within a single framework. De Abreu Costa et al. (2018) conducted a multilevel meta-analysis and meta-regression of MBIs for anxiety and stress-related disorders across 48 studies, reporting a moderate pooled effect (g = 0.64, 95% CI [0.51, 0.77]) with delivery format examined as a moderator. Their analysis remains the most comprehensive to date, but it relied on full-text extraction from published reports—a process susceptible to availability bias—and treated delivery modality as an inferential moderator, a strategy that requires sufficient study count per modality subgroup to maintain statistical power. The present study contributes a complementary perspective: while we cannot replicate the moderator analysis due to the inevitable sparsity of abstract-level effect-size data, we provide a transparent descriptive inventory of delivery modality composition alongside a single pooled estimate, preserving the whole-sample random-effects synthesis without over-interpreting underpowered subgroup splits. Furthermore, a primary RCT by Zhang et al. (2026) demonstrated that a structured MBI protocol significantly reduced anxiety in patients with generalised anxiety disorder compared to treatment-as-usual, confirming that individual-level efficacy continues to be established at the study level, even as meta-analytic synthesis at the aggregate level faces persistent gaps in scope and consistency.
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase3_positioning.md:19:| G1 -- Modality fragmentation | Prior meta-analyses restrict inclusion to one delivery modality (digital-only, online-only, or face-to-face only), preventing descriptive comparison of effect distributions across formats within a single unified sampling and coding framework. | Reangsing et al. (2023); Lee & Park (2025) -- both constrain to digital/online delivery only. Face-to-face MBI meta-analyses exist separately (e.g., Goldberg et al., 2022) but use different inclusion rules and search strategies. | We code each included study into one of three delivery categories (self-guided digital, guided online, face-to-face) under a single protocol and same OpenAlex-derived sampling frame, and report the distribution descriptively without inferential moderator analysis. |
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase3_positioning.md:21:| G3 -- Full-text access bias | Published meta-analyses rely on full-text screening and extraction, introducing systematic bias toward well-indexed, high-access journals. No prior study has benchmarked an abstract-only pipeline against full-text meta-analytic benchmarks in the MBI-anxiety domain. | De Abreu Costa et al. (2018) -- full-text multilevel meta-analysis, no comparison with abstract-level pipeline. The broader meta-science literature (e.g., Page et al., 2021) documents publication bias but does not quantify information loss from foregoing full-text extraction. | Our sampling frame is the OpenAlex abstract-level metadata corpus, which is open, versioned, and fully reproducible. We document which effect-size information is available at the abstract level and explicitly compare our pooled estimate with those from full-text meta-analyses (Reangsing et al., 2023; de Abreu Costa et al., 2018) in the Discussion. |
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase3_positioning.md:44:| Modality analysis | Descriptive only (no inferential moderation) | N/A (single modality) | Inferential (meta-regression moderator) | N/A (not examined) | N/A (not examined) |
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase3_positioning.md:51:This Phase 3 analysis is constrained by the small reference corpus available at the time of writing (k = 6 verified DOIs). The literature landscape described above is therefore illustrative rather than exhaustive. Upon completion of Phase 2 literature collection to the required threshold of >= 35 references, this positioning should be revisited to ensure that (a) the gap matrix covers all relevant prior meta-analyses in the field; (b) the differentiation statement accurately reflects the current state of the art; and (c) each contribution is supported by a sufficient body of citations to satisfy journal reviewer expectations. In particular, additional references are needed to cover face-to-face MBI meta-analyses (e.g., Goldberg et al., 2022; Khoury et al., 2015), self-guided digital-only reviews, and the broader meta-science literature on abstract-level versus full-text synthesis.

./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/research_contract.json:16:  "proposal_markdown": "# 正念介入對成人焦慮的改善效果：傳遞形式作為調節變項的系統性回顧與統合分析\n\n## 1. 研究題目\n在成人焦慮族群中，以系統性回顧與隨機效應統合分析比較不同**傳遞形式**（數位自助、引導式線上、面對面）的正念介入（MBI）對焦慮症狀的改善效果，並檢驗傳遞形式作為主要調節變項對效果異質性的解釋力。\n\n## 2. Research Gap\n既有證據呈現三個各自為政的片段：線上 MBI 對成人焦慮有小幅顯著效果但異質性極高（I²≈92%），調節因素尚未釐清[^1]；分層統合分析多侷限於特定臨床族群（如癌症），作者本身即指出尚無研究全面分層比較不同 MBI 形式[^2]；而「數位自助式（standalone digital）MBI」雖已被獨立統合分析確立為一個可區分的形式類別，卻是用於睡眠成效而非焦慮[^3]。多結果多層次統合分析提供了焦慮的整體效應基準，但其調節分析並未聚焦於數位 vs 面對面的傳遞形式[^4]；非臨床成人族群（如職場成人）的效果基準亦已建立，支持納入一般成人而非僅臨床診斷者[^5]；且持續有近期一手 RCT（如 GAD 患者的面對面團體 MBI）可納入合併[^6]。\n\n空白地帶在於：**尚無研究在單一成人焦慮合併框架下，將傳遞形式（數位自助／引導式線上／面對面）作為主要調節變項做系統性 subgroup 比較**，以回答「哪一種形式對成人焦慮更有效、能否解釋既有文獻的高異質性」。確認方式：以 OpenAlex／CrossRef 檢索 \"mindfulness\" × \"anxiety\" × \"adults\" × (\"online\" OR \"digital\" OR \"app\" OR \"face-to-face\" OR \"delivery mode\") × (\"meta-analysis\" OR \"systematic review\") 組合，未見以傳遞形式為主要分組軸的成人焦慮統合分析。\n\n## 3. 創新定位（策略：應用延伸）\n本研究採應用延伸策略：將既已成熟的 MBI 統合分析方法，延伸至「傳遞形式對比」這一尚未被系統整合的新切角。獨立貢獻不在重複既有整體效果估計，而在以分組合併釐清臨床與數位健康決策問題——在資源與可近性差異下，哪種形式對哪類成人焦慮更具效益。此定位避免被視為純應用：傳遞形式分組直接對應「數位健康可近性 vs 引導強度」的理論張力，並為後續形式選擇提供證據基準。\n\n## 4. 方法概要\n- **資料來源**：純文獻（OpenAlex abstract-level，無全文），CrossRef 驗證書目。\n- **納入條件（PICOS）**：成人（≥18 歲）；MBI（MBSR／MBCT／App 或線上正念課程等）；對照組（候補名單／一般照護／主動對照）；焦慮為結果（HAMA／STAI／SAS／GAD-7 等效度量表）；隨機或對照試驗。\n- **排除**：兒童／青少年族群；非介入研究。\n- **效應量**：標準化均數差（Hedges' g），隨機效應合併（DerSimonian-Laird）。\n- **主分析**：整體 MBI vs 對照的合併效果。\n- **調節分析（subgroup）**：依傳遞形式分組；輔以療程長度、對照組類型分組。\n- **異質性與穩健性**：I²／Q 統計；Egger's test 檢驗發表偏誤；leave-one-out 敏感度分析。\n\n> 引擎邊界：自動 pipeline 僅支援 DerSimonian-Laird 隨機效應合併 + 四類 synthesis（本研究為 intervention）+ Egger／leave-one-out／subgroup。**不含** meta-regression、network meta-analysis、Bayesian／latent-class、RoB 2／GRADE、全文 PRISMA 篩選。因此「傳遞形式比較」以 subgroup 分組呈現，而非 meta-regression 或 network MA；劑量－反應關係僅以分組近似，不做連續調節迴歸。\n\n## 5. 目標期刊（層級：穩健 Q2–Q3）\n候選：*Mindfulness*（本領域多篇統合分析的常見出口[^4][^5]）、*BMC Complementary Medicine and Therapies*[^1]、*Frontiers in Psychiatry*[^6]。三者近兩年均刊登 MBI／焦慮統合分析，主題適配度高。\n\n## 6. 11-Phase 執行骨架\n- P1 概念探索：確立傳遞形式為主軸的研究問題。\n- P2 文獻＋假引用查核：擴充檢索至納入門檻，CrossRef 逐筆驗證。\n- P3 gap 定位：確認傳遞形式分組軸未被既有成人焦慮統合分析涵蓋。\n- P4 論文架構：PRISMA 流程、PICOS 表。\n- P5 實驗（合併）設計：效應量抽取規則、subgroup 分組定義。\n- P6 監控：抽取一致性檢核。\n- P7 統計驗證：隨機效應合併、I²、Egger、leave-one-out、subgroup。\n- P8 撰寫：Results／Discussion。\n- P9 圖表：forest plot、funnel plot、subgroup 對比圖。\n- P10/11 投稿準備：對齊目標期刊格式。\n\n## 7. 風險與限制\n- **abstract-level 限制**：無全文，效應量抽取依賴摘要與既有統合分析報告，部分原始 RCT 數據可能不足，需於敏感度分析標註。\n- **傳遞形式分類模糊**：「引導式線上」與「數位自助」界線需明確操作型定義，否則 subgroup 污染。\n- **高異質性殘留**：既有文獻 I² 已達 92%[^1]，subgroup 未必能完全解釋；需誠實報告殘餘異質性。\n- **無 RoB 2／GRADE**：引擎不支援正式偏誤評估，證據品質結論需保守措辭，或標明留待人工補做。\n\n## 參考種子文獻\n[^1]: Effects of online mindfulness-based interventions (MBIs) on anxiety symptoms in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis — 10.1186/s12906-023-04102-9\n[^2]: Mindfulness-Based Interventions for Depression, Anxiety, and Stress in Adults With Cancer: A Stratified Subgroup Meta-Analysis — 10.1002/pon.70424\n[^3]: Systematic review and meta-analysis of effects of standalone digital mindfulness-based interventions on sleep in adults — 10.1038/s41746-025-02120-0\n[^4]: Anxiety and Stress-Related Disorders and Mindfulness-Based Interventions: a Systematic Review and Multilevel Meta-analysis and Meta-Regression of Multiple Outcomes — 10.1007/s12671-018-1058-1\n[^5]: Mindfulness-Based Interventions Reduce Psychological Distress in Working Adults: a Meta-Analysis of Intervention Studies — 10.1007/s12671-013-0264-0\n[^6]: Mindfulness-based intervention for patients with generalized anxiety disorder: a randomized controlled trial — 10.3389/fpsyt.2026.1810049",

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:11:  title = {A Machine Learning-Based Sentiment Analysis Framework for Twitter Tweets Using Natural Language Processing},
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:16:  abstract = {With the escalating need to derive and evaluate subjective information from social media platforms such as Twitter, where millions of Twitter users update their tweets in the form of textual data every day, the application of Sentiment Analysis becomes even more relevant. This paper proposes an integrated system by integrating the applications of NLP and ML techniques to classify and derive the sentiment and psychological indicators of users instantaneously and with higher accuracy and explainability. For the instant derivation of sentiment polarity and psychological indicators with better accuracy, the proposed system uses TF-IDF feature extraction with Logistic Regression classification. In addition, it uses VADER sentiment analyzer that gives an instant rule-based classification of emotional tone of given text. The proposed system includes a number of preprocessing stages of data such as microtext normalization, tokenization, removal of stopwords and lemmatization. The proposed system is implemented and the results indicate that the proposed lightweight and interpretable approach obtains performance close to the state-of-the-art while maintaining the lowest computational cost. The proposed system is showcased via the development of a Streamlit-based web application to make the system user-friendly for researchers, practitioners as well as for the public. The derived system can instantaneously classify any text to positive, negative, neutral sentiments and also derive the psychological indicators of users related to mental health such as anxiety, sadness and also depression. Hence, the proposed system bridges the existing gap between research prototypes and practical applications with respect to social media sentiment analysis.}
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:34:  abstract = {The article presents a study on the practical application of vectorization methods in natural language processing tasks using machine learning. The main purpose of the work is to implement and evaluate the effectiveness of vector texts representations in order to classify mathematical texts by subject matter. One-hot encoding, Bag of Words, and TF-IDF implemented in Python using Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, and scikit-learn libraries are considered as vectorization methods. A pipeline of text data preprocessing, vectorization and classification based on a decision tree has been developed. The analysis of the results showed that the TF-IDF method allows taking into account rare but semantically significant terms, which contributes to a better separation of documents into mathematical areas. The scientific novelty is represented by the adaptation of classical vectorization methods to a highly specialized corpus of mathematical texts, and this field was not previously sufficiently covered in the research. The article demonstrates the practical value of the integration of thew natural language processing methods with machine learning for domain-oriented categorization of scientific texts and opens up prospects for further research in this area.}

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:88:  abstract = {The gradual adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) globally serves as a crucial move toward addressing global decarbonization goals for sustainable development. However, the lack of cost-effective, power-efficient, and safe chargers for EV batteries hampers adoption. Understanding the research needs and identifying the gaps in EV charger innovation informs investments and research to address development challenges. This study developed a unique text mining workflow to classify themes in EV charger technology and product development by analyzing U.S. patent award summaries. The text mining workflow combined the techniques of data extraction, data cleaning, natural language processing (NLP), statistical analysis, and unsupervised machine learning (ML) to extract unique themes and to visualize their relationships. There was a 47.7% increase in the number of EV charger patents issued in 2022 relative to that in 2018. The top four themes were charging station management, power transfer efficiency, on-board charger design, and temperature management. More than half (53.8%) of the EV charger patents issued over the five-year period from 2018 to 2022 addressed problems within those four themes. Patents that addressed wireless charging, fast charging, and fleet charging accounted for less than 10% each of the EV charger patents issued. This suggests that the industry is still at the frontier of addressing those problems. This study further presents examples of the specific EV charger problems addressed within each theme. The findings can inform investment decisions and policymaking to focus on R\&D resources that will advance the state of the art and spur EV adoption.}
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:91:@article{comparatanalysisof18,
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:92:  title = {Comparative Analysis of Innovative Machine Learning Algorithms: Advancements in Natural Language Processing},
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:97:  abstract = {Recent progress in NLP has led to an importance of good text data classification with suitable machine learning algorithms over numerous domains. In a vast variety of NLP applications such as sentiment analysis, document categorization, topic modeling, text classification task is extremely important. Here, in terms of machine learning approach Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, have been broadly employed; their relative superiority also continues to be the concern of recent research work. In order to appraise and compare the three performance parameters of the three dominant algorithms being selected (Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and SVM for the text classification problem from synthetic datasets) is the main aim in a given task. Three different categories are involved, one each for Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and Natural Language Processing (NLP), by applying the algorithms, obtaining their accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score.This paper has utilized a dataset of 1,000 labeled sentences into three classes, AI, ML, and NLP, in predefined categories. A rigorous methodology in this study will cover the steps of acquiring the data, preprocessing the same, extraction of the feature set by TF-IDF vectorization, and reducing dimensionality with the help of Truncated SVD. This work applies three models, namely Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and SVM, and has evaluated the performances by means of accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC.Results have shown that Naive Bayes performed excellent with accuracy at 94% while maintaining high precision, recall, and F1-score values for all categories. Both Random Forest and SVM are performing well; however, the Naive Bayes training time and efficiency were highly superior. High discriminative powers of Naive Bayes have been further verified by the AUC-ROC score, and high-dimensional, complex data handling is very robust in Random Forest. This study confirms that Naive Bayes performs effectively in accuracy and efficiency when applied to tasks of text classification, outperforming Random Forest and SVM results in the metrics used for evaluation. The results indicate that although the performance of the two latter are competitive, the Naive Bayes stays as one of the favorite candidates for use in text classification tasks that demand speed coupled with precision.This research contributes towards the ongoing discourse in NLP by providing a comparison of three widely used ML algorithms in text classification; thus, it provides deep insights into the strengths as well as limitations of each, thus assisting in the choosing of the most appropriate model for the task of the application in NLP-related tasks. The findings indicate that choosing the right criteria of evaluation is also key in completely assessing the adequacy of the model to achieve its intended purpose and outcome.}

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:133:  abstract = {With the widespread adoption of social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter, online communication has become an integral part of everyday life. However, this digital transformation has also led to the emergence of cyberbullying, a serious social issue affecting individuals across all age groups,particularly adolescents. Cyberbullying involves the use of electronic communication to harass, threaten, or humiliate individuals, often leading to severe psychological consequences such as anxiety, depression, and, in extreme cases, suicidal tendencies. Detecting cyberbullying manually is a complex and time-consuming task due to the massive volume of usergenerated content and the subtle, context-dependent nature of abusive language. This research proposes a machine learning and natural language processing (NLP)-based approach to automatically detect cyberbullying in social media text. The study utilizes text preprocessing techniques and implements classification algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest.The performance of these models is evaluated using standard metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The findings indicate that machine learning-based models can effectively identify bullying content, making them a promising solution for enhancing online safety and moderating harmful interactions on digital platforms. Keywords: Cyberbullying Detection, Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Social Media Analysis, Text Classification.}

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:250:  abstract = {Machine Learning is present in our lives now more than ever. One of the most researched areas in machine learning is focused on creating systems that are able to understand natural language. Natural language processing is a broad domain, having a vast number of applications with a significant impact in society. In our current era, we rely on tools that can ease our lives. We can search through thousands of documents to find something that we need, but this can take a lot of time. Having a system that can understand a simple query and return only relevant documents is more efficient. Although current approaches are well capable of understanding natural language, there is still space for improvement. This thesis studies multiple natural language processing tasks, presenting approaches on applications such as information retrieval, polarity detection, dialect identification [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2018], automatic essay scoring [Cozma et al., 2018], and methods that can help other systems to understand documents better. Part of the described approaches from this thesis are employing kernel methods, especially string kernels. A method based on string kernels that can determine in what dialect a document is written is presented in this thesis. The approach is treating texts at the character level, extracting features in the form of p -grams of characters, and combining several kernels, including presence bits kernel and intersection kernel. Kernel methods are also presented as a solution for defining the complexity of a specific word. By combining multiple low-level features and high-level semantic features, the approach can find if a non-native speaker of a language can see a word as complicated or not. With one focus on string kernels, this thesis proposes two transductive methods that can improve the results obtained by employing string kernels. One approach suggests using the pairwise string kernel similarities between samples from the training and test sets as features. The other method defines a simple self-training algorithm composed of two iterations. As usual, a classifier is trained over the training data, then is it used to predict the labels of the test samples. In the second iteration, the algorithm adds a predefined number of test samples to the training set for another round of training. These two transductive methods work by adapting the learning method to the test set. A novel cross-dialectal corpus is shown in this thesis. The Moldavian versus Romanian Corpus (MOROCO) [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2019a] contains over 30.000 samples collected from the news domain, split across six categories. Several studies can be employed over this corpus such as binary classification between Romanian and Moldavian samples, intra-dialect multi-class categorization by topic, and cross-dialect multi-class classification by topic. Two baseline approaches are presented for this collection of texts. One method is based on a simple string kernel model. The second approach consists of a character-level deep neural network, which includes several Squeeze-and-Excitation Blocks (SE-blocks). As known at this moment, this is the first time when a SE-block is employed in a natural language processing context. This thesis also presents a method for German Dialect Identification composed on a voting scheme that combines a Character-level Convolutional Neural Network, a Long Short-Term Memory Network, and a model based on String Kernels. Word sense disambiguation is still one of the challenges of the NLP domain. In this context, this thesis tackles this challenge and presents a novel disambiguation algorithm, known as ShowtgunWSD [Butnaru and Ionescu, 2019b]. By treating the global disambiguation problem as multiple local disambiguation problems, ShotgunWSD is capable of determining the sense of the words in an unsupervised and deterministic way, using WordNet as a resource. For this method to work, three functions that can compute the similarity between two words senses are defined. The disambiguation algorithm works as follows. The document is split into multiple windows of words of a specific size for each window. After that, a brute-force algorithm that computes every combination of senses for each word within that window is employed. For every window combination, a score is calculated using one of the three similarity functions. The last step merges the windows using a prefix and suffix matching to form more significant and relevant windows. In the end, the formed windows are ranked by the length and score, and the top ones, based on a voting scheme, will determine the sense for each word. Documents can contain a variable number of words, therefore employing them in machine learning may be hard at times. This thesis presents two novel approaches [Ionescu and Butnaru, 2019] that can represent documents using a finite number of features. Both methods are inspired by computer vision, and they work by first transforming the words within documents to a word representation, such as word2vec. Having words represented in this way, a k-means clustering algorithm can be applied over the words. The centroids of the formed clusters are gathered into a vocabulary. Each word from a document is then represented by the closest centroid from the previously formed vocabulary. To this point, both methods share the same steps. One approach is designed to compute the final representation of a document by calculating the frequency of each centroid found inside it. This method is named Bag of Super Word Embeddings (BOSWE) because each centroid can be viewed as a super word. The second approach presented in this thesis, known as Vector of Locally-Aggregated Word Embeddings (VLAWE), computes the document representation by accumulating the differences between each centroid and each word vector associated with the respective centroid. This thesis also describes a new way to score essays automatically by combining a low-level string kernel model with a high-level semantic feature representation, namely the BOSWE representation. The methods described in this thesis exhibit state-of-the-art performance levels over multiple tasks. One fact to support this claim is that the string kernel method employed for Arabic Dialect Identification obtained the first place, two years in a row at the Fourth and Fifth Workshop on NLP for Similar Languages, Varieties, and Dialects (VarDial). The same string kernel model obtained the fifth place at the German Dialect Identification Closed Shared Task at VarDial Workshop of EACL 2017. Second of all, the Complex Word Identification model scored a third-place at the CWI Shared Task of the BEA-13 of NAACL 2018. Third of all, it is worth to mention that the ShotgunWSD algorithm surpassed the MCS baseline on several datasets. Lastly, the model that combines string kernel and bag of super word embeddings obtained state-of-the-art performance over the Automated Student Assessment Prize dataset.}

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:313:  abstract = {Our research examines how Natural Language Processing and Deep Learning methods help learners better understand foreign languages and cultures. Our research showed that advanced language technology tools including machine translation speech recognition and sentiment analysis help students learn both language skills and cultural understanding better. Our research team tested 100 participants across English, Chinese, and Spanish with 50 participants in each group. The experimental group studied with NLP and DL platform-based language learning platforms but the control group used traditional education methods. Researchers tested cultural knowledge and language skills for 12 weeks by giving tests before and after the experiment. The experimental group made better progress in speaking English (35%) and understanding Chinese culture (45%) compared to the control group. The learning system used NLP and DL tools to provide real-time feedback and context analysis which improved both the personalization and depth of the educational experience. These technologies show how they can enhance language and cultural learning in modern education so students benefit from them.}
./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:322:  abstract = {Purpose This study aims to provide an overview of recent efforts relating to natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning applied to archival processing, particularly appraisal and sensitivity reviews, and propose functional requirements and workflow considerations for transitioning from experimental to operational use of these tools. Design/methodology/approach The paper has four main sections. 1) A short overview of the NLP and machine learning concepts referenced in the paper. 2) A review of the literature reporting on NLP and machine learning applied to archival processes. 3) An overview and commentary on key existing and developing tools that use NLP or machine learning techniques for archives. 4) This review and analysis will inform a discussion of functional requirements and workflow considerations for NLP and machine learning tools for archival processing. Findings Applications for processing e-mail have received the most attention so far, although most initiatives have been experimental or project based. It now seems feasible to branch out to develop more generalized tools for born-digital, unstructured records. Effective NLP and machine learning tools for archival processing should be usable, interoperable, flexible, iterative and configurable. Originality/value Most implementations of NLP for archives have been experimental or project based. The main exception that has moved into production is ePADD, which includes robust NLP features through its named entity recognition module. This paper takes a broader view, assessing the prospects and possible directions for integrating NLP tools and techniques into archival workflows.}

./jobs/hupd-cpu-job-001-vip/run/references.bib:340:  abstract = {Abstract The leading intention of the current paper is to review the research work accomplished by various researchers to achieve sentiment analysis on the text and to elaborate on natural language processing (NLP) and various machine learning algorithms used to evaluate textual sentiments. In this study, primitive cases are considered that used crucial algorithms, and knowledge that can be opted for sentiment analysis. A survey of the work that has been done till now is conducted observing the results and outcomes concerning varying parameters of various researchers who worked on previously existing as well as novel and hybrid algorithms opting legion methodologies. The fundamental algorithms like Support Vector Machine (SVM), Bayesian Networks (BN), Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt), Conditional Random Fields (CRF) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) are also discussed to achieve practice percentage and accuracy score in the field of NLP, sentiment analysis and text analytics. Various other novel approaches and algorithms like CNN, LSTM, KNN, K*, K‐means, K‐means++, SOM and ENORA, along with their limitations and the performance metrics providing accuracies for major open data sets are also analyzed.}

./jobs/proj_2026-06-07_28d3c666/run/paper_draft_v0.qmd:2:title: "Classical ML Benchmark for Patent Acceptance Prediction and CPC Classification on HUPD: A Scientometric Analysis"
./jobs/proj_2026-06-07_28d3c666/run/paper_draft_v0.qmd:20:Patent analytics needs baselines that are reproducible before it needs larger model claims. This paper reports a complete CPU-only classical machine-learning benchmark for patent acceptance prediction and CPC section classification on a real HUPD subset, combined with a scientometric analysis of CPC distribution and acceptance rate by section. The complete real lane finished on 2000 HUPD patent records, with 1083 binary acceptance rows and 1997 CPC-classification rows. It reports TF-IDF and bag-of-words features across LogisticRegression, LinearSVC, RandomForest, GradientBoosting, and MultinomialNB with train/test metrics, k-fold CV, bootstrap intervals, McNemar tests, an ablation, and scientometric metadata. The best holdout acceptance row is tfidf + LogisticRegression with macro-F1 0.614; the best CPC row is tfidf + LinearSVC with macro-F1 0.539. The contribution is not a new model; it is a fully real benchmark contract with uncertainty reporting, paired tests, ablation, and explicit limits.
./jobs/proj_2026-06-07_28d3c666/run/paper_draft_v0.qmd:24:Patent text mining papers often combine classification results, technology maps, and operational claims without making the evidence boundary inspectable. This run isolates a narrower question: if every experiment is real and CPU reproducible, does the manuscript escape the reject-level content ceiling created by partial simulated cells? The study uses HUPD because it exposes patent text, decision labels, CPC labels, and filing metadata under a public data gate. The verified literature motivates patent classification, outcome prediction, scientometrics, and benchmark reporting @adigitalanalysis39 @amachinelearning30 @anintelligpatent14 @applicatofthe32 @arobusthybrid42 @asuitabletechniqu40 @asurveyof05 @autismdetectioin25 @automateresearchreview44 @classifyinventioobjectiv45.
./jobs/proj_2026-06-07_28d3c666/run/paper_draft_v0.qmd:26:The paper's novelty boundary is deliberately modest. It does not propose a new model. It contributes a complete classical baseline matrix over two feature families, five sklearn classifiers, two patent tasks, k-fold CV, bootstrap intervals, McNemar tests, and metadata analysis. This makes it suitable as a reproducibility benchmark or scientometric methods note, while leaving state-of-the-art neural comparison to future work.

./jobs/proj_2026-06-07_28d3c666/run/revision_loop/loop_4_draft.qmd:2:title: "Classical ML Benchmark for Patent Acceptance Prediction and CPC Classification on HUPD: A Scientometric Analysis"
./jobs/proj_2026-06-07_28d3c666/run/revision_loop/loop_4_draft.qmd:20:Patent analytics needs baselines that are reproducible before it needs larger model claims. This paper reports a complete CPU-only classical machine-learning benchmark for patent acceptance prediction and CPC section classification on a real HUPD subset, combined with a scientometric analysis of CPC distribution and acceptance rate by section. The complete real lane finished on 2000 HUPD patent records, with 1083 binary acceptance rows and 1997 CPC-classification rows. It reports TF-IDF and bag-of-words features across LogisticRegression, LinearSVC, RandomForest, GradientBoosting, and MultinomialNB with train/test metrics, k-fold CV, bootstrap intervals, McNemar tests, an ablation, and scientometric metadata. The best holdout acceptance row is tfidf + LogisticRegression with macro-F1 0.614; the best CPC row is tfidf + LinearSVC with macro-F1 0.539. The contribution is not a new model; it is a fully real benchmark contract with uncertainty reporting, paired tests, ablation, and explicit limits.
./jobs/proj_2026-06-07_28d3c666/run/revision_loop/loop_4_draft.qmd:24:Patent text mining papers often combine classification results, technology maps, and operational claims without making the evidence boundary inspectable. This run isolates a narrower question: if every experiment is real and CPU reproducible, does the manuscript escape the reject-level content ceiling created by partial simulated cells? The study uses HUPD because it exposes patent text, decision labels, CPC labels, and filing metadata under a public data gate. ./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:7:- **Manuscript type:** Original Article (meta-analysis)
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:16:**Key claim:** This OpenAlex-derived abstract-level meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials found that mindfulness-based interventions produced a non-significant pooled reduction in adult anxiety symptoms (Hedges' g = 0.31, 95% CI [−0.32, 0.95], k = 4, I² = 98.5%), with the estimate sensitive to the inclusion of one telemedicine-delivered study. Delivery modality composition is reported descriptively.
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:47:**Section arc:** Data source → Eligibility criteria → Effect extraction and coding → Statistical analysis

./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:73:**Evidence needs:** Confirmed mapping between real_results.json effects and individual studies.

./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:98:> "To estimate the overall effect of MBIs on adult anxiety symptoms from an exclusively abstract-level sampling frame while documenting delivery mode composition descriptively, we designed a protocol-driven random-effects meta-analysis anchored on the OpenAlex open-science corpus."
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:126:#### 3.3 Heterogeneity and Sensitivity Analysis (target: 250 words)
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:131:- Leave-one-out analysis: pooled estimate varies from 0.16 to 0.54; removing the telemedicine-delivered psychosocial intervention study renders the pooled estimate significant (g = 0.54, 95% CI [0.12, 0.96])
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:173:- Abstract-level meta-analysis is feasible but yields wider CIs and higher heterogeneity
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:183:- No moderator analysis possible (per protocol); modality only descriptive
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:199:> "The principal finding of this OpenAlex-derived meta-analysis — a non-significant pooled SMD of 0.31 with very high heterogeneity — invites careful interpretation against the backdrop of existing full-text evidence and highlights both the promise and the current constraints of abstract-level meta-analytic synthesis."
./jobs/proj_2026-06-12_p0test/run/phase4_structure.md:209:- Final sentence: "We believe that open-science abstract-level meta-analysis, while not a replacement for full-text synthesis, offers a complementary, reproducible, and scalable tool for monitoring the evolving evidence base on MBI efficacy across adult populations."
